intro: Arkansas Legislative Audit examines every county and publishes what it finds. This page quotes what the auditors reported about Jackson County, from its latest report — no verdict added in either direction. What the auditors said is the record; what to make of it is yours.
regulatory_basis_note: Read this before reading any Arkansas audit: county and city reports carry a technical 'adverse opinion' on GAAP grounds because Arkansas law has them keep books on a simpler 'regulatory basis.' That phrase appears in every such audit in the state and signals the accounting format — not wrongdoing. A report is 'clean' or not in its findings, deficiencies, and noncompliance sections, which is what this page quotes.

verdicts.quote: The results of our tests disclosed no instances of noncompliance or other matters that are required to be reported under Government Auditing Standards.
verdicts.detail: On internal control, the auditors wrote: “During our audit we did not identify any deficiencies in internal control that we consider to be material weaknesses.”

verdicts.quote: The following deficiencies were noted during the review of the Circuit Clerk's office: • The Fee, Receipting, and Fidlar bank reconciliations were not always prepared in accordance with Ark. Code Ann. § 14-25-107. • The Receipting and Fidlar journals contained posting errors related to beginning cash balances, receipting, disbursements, and ending cash balances.
verdicts.detail: The auditors also reported these matters to county officials in a separate letter. The letter continues in the report on page 8; parts that concern staff positions are left to the report, since this site doesn’t single out non-elected staff.

limits: From the 2024 report, dated September 18, 2025. Read by machine from the report’s text; the quotes are the auditors’ words. Older reports, and the separate federal (single) audits, aren’t on this page yet.
Arkansas alternates between full audits and limited “financial and compliance” reviews; each line says which this is.

cities.quote: Noncompliance with state law and accepted accounting practices was noted in the office of Mayor. Mayor Restricted Street Fund revenue of $11,000 was used to replace septic tanks on two private properties in apparent noncompliance with Ark. Code Ann. §§ 26-79-104, 27-70-207 and in apparent conflict with Ark.

cities.name: Diaz
cities.quote: Noncompliance with state law and accepted accounting practices was noted in the office of Recorder/Treasurer. Recorder/Treasurer The General Fund bank account was not reconciled accurately at the end of each month. Additionally, the bank reconciliations were not prepared promptly at the end of each month for the Act 833 and Fire Department accounts, in noncompliance with Ark. Code Ann.

cities.name: Grubbs
cities.quote: Noncompliance with state law and accepted accounting practices were noted in the offices of Mayor and Recorder/Treasurer. Mayor The City entered into a seven year financed purchase agreement on September 17, 2024, in the amount of $37,356, for the purchase of a tractor and rotary cutter, which appears to be in conflict with Ark. Const. amend.

cities.name: Jacksonport
cities.quote: Noncompliance with state law and accepted accounting practices was noted in the office of Recorder/Treasurer. Recorder/Treasurer 1. Prenumbered receipts were not issued for all funds received, in noncompliance with Ark. Code Ann.

cities.name: Newport
cities.quote: Noncompliance with state law and accepted accounting practices was noted in the offices of Mayor and Clerk/Treasurer. Mayor and Clerk/Treasurer During review of unused leave payments for retirement or other separation, we identified the following issues: • Two individuals were paid a total of $1,673 for unused vacation leave, in excess of the maximum allowed by City policy. • One individual was underpaid $849 for unused vacation leave, in noncompliance with Ark. Code Ann.

cities.name: Tuckerman
cities.quote: Noncompliance with state law and accepted accounting practices was noted in the office of Recorder/Treasurer. Recorder/Treasurer Restricted funds from previous years of $68,562 were not transferred from the General Fund to the Fire Truck Fund, as required by City of Tuckerman Ordinance no. 2006-3 (April 11, 2006). On January 13, 2025, the City passed Resolution 014-2024 for the General Fund to pay $1,000 per month to the Fire Truck Fund until the balance is paid in full.

cities.name: Tupelo

cities.name: Weldon
cities.quote: Noncompliance with state law and accepted accounting practices was noted in the office of Recorder/Treasurer. Recorder/Treasurer Bank accounts for the General and Volunteer Fire Funds were not properly reconciled, and reconciliations were not properly approved by someone other than the preparer, as required by Ark. Code Ann. § 14-59-108.
